bindings.statement: The catalog's conductance drift law does not depend on the reference time, and its exponent is minus the slope of log G against log t_d. Its thermionic conductance is the zero-bias slope of the Richardson-Dushman current; with an ideality factor n that slope is G/n in the form I_s (exp(q_e V/(n k_B T)) - 1) and G in the form I_s exp(q_e V/(n k_B T)) (1 - exp(-q_e V/(k_B T))), and the barrier follows exactly from conductances at two temperatures. Its retention time is the mean exit time of a constant-rate escape, divided by M for M exit paths, and the barrier follows exactly from retention times at two temperatures. Under a linear voltage ramp the expected hop count from zero bias is the leading term minus g_r k_B T/(alpha_F tau_ret); the leading term is exp((V - V*)/b), b = k_B T/alpha_F, equal to one at the catalog's location V*, and the first-hop voltage with survival exp(-exp((V - V*)/b)) has mean V* - gamma b, the catalog's set voltage. Its programming error equals the per-cell model it was written from, decreases strictly as the conductance window widens, tends to c sqrt(S_2/2)/S_1, and exceeds c/sqrt(2 n_w) for every kernel and window. For a conductance that rises (or falls) monotonically during a pulse, the dissipated energy lies between the catalog's pulse energies at the initial and the final conductance. For a channel of segments in series, the catalog's conductance with the length-averaged conductivity is an upper bound on the true conductance.
conditions: Energies Phi_Bn and E_m are in joules, T in kelvin, k_B and q_e exact SI; P_th in A/K^2, G in siemens, nu_0 in THz and g_r in ps/V as the catalog stores them. An energy in eV read as joules is wrong by a factor 1.6e-19.
Drift: G_0 is nonzero and all times are positive; the law is the fitted power law inside the time range where nu was fitted.

Thermionic: one contact, thermionic emission over the barrier without field emission, the three-dimensional T^2 Richardson law, small signal |V| much smaller than k_B T/q_e; the catalog's G is the slope for ideality factor 1, and for an ideality factor n the slope is G/n or G depending on the form of the current law; Phi_Bn is the effective zero-bias barrier. The two-temperature inversion assumes Phi_Bn and P_th independent of temperature for the same contact.

Retention: one back-hop path at the Arrhenius rate nu_0 exp(-E_m/(k_B T)), or M equivalent paths; the two-temperature inversion assumes E_m and nu_0 independent of temperature. At one temperature E_m and nu_0 cannot be separated.

Ramp: a linear ramp with dwell g_r per volt (1/ramp rate, or t_p/dV for a staircase), alpha_F > 0, a barrier falling linearly with V, one hop switching the device, the device at temperature T. The mean set voltage uses the leading hop count and neglects hops at zero and negative bias, whose expected number g_r k_B T/(alpha_F tau_ret) must be much smaller than one.

Programming error: the per-cell model of the catalog description with c > 0, W > 1, w_max > 0, n_w the count of nonzero weights, S_1 = sum |w_i| and S_2 = sum w_i^2. Read noise, drift, IR drop, sneak paths and correlated errors are not included.

Pulse energy: G is the chord conductance I(V_p)/V_p and changes monotonically during the pulse (rising for SET, falling for RESET); the bracket holds for any width t_p >= 0 in the catalog's time unit.

Device conductance: current flows along the channel through segments of positive length and conductivity with one cross-section A; the catalog's sigma is then the length-averaged conductivity and the catalog conductance an upper bound, equal for a uniform channel.

bindings.statement: The weighted least-squares slope of log D against 1/T returns the activation energy exactly, E_a = -k_B times the slope, on data that follow the catalog's Arrhenius law, for every choice of positive weights and at least two distinct temperatures. bindings.statement: With the relaxation-time mean free displacement F = v/(2 Gamma) and, as c, the actual Physlib canonical heat capacity of each harmonic mode at T > 0, the OMAI contraction kappa_ab = sum_m F_b c v_a/(N_q V_cell) is symmetric and positive semidefinite for positive linewidths and N_q V_cell > 0, and positive definite exactly when the group velocities of the modes span space.
conditions: MeanFreeDisplacement[bte_solver=rta] is F_a = v_a/(2 Gamma) from solve_bte[bte_solver=rta], with Gamma the total half-width Im Sigma (phono3py's gamma), positive for every mode, so 1/tau = 2 Gamma. ShengBTE and kALDo report 1/tau, which must be halved before use as Gamma.

HeatCapacity is, for each mode, the derivative-defined heat capacity of the full Nat harmonic-oscillator canonical ensemble of Physlib at the mode's positive angular frequency and T > 0, as in the harmonic-mode-heat-capacity binding. The oscillator mass does not enter.
N_q and V_cell are positive; the mode sum is finite.
Positive definiteness holds exactly when, for every nonzero direction x, some mode has v.x != 0. A crystal whose velocities all lie in a plane gives a semidefinite, singular kappa.

bindings.statement: Both closed-form branches of the catalog's spheroid depolarization factor and its sphere value equal int_0^1 t^2/(t^2 + p^2 (1 - t^2)) dt, so L33 lies in (0, 1), decreases strictly with the aspect ratio, is continuous through the sphere p = 1 with value 1/3, tends to 0 for needles and to 1 for disks. For every spheroid shape and volume fraction in [0, 1], the catalog's random Nan conductivity exceeds the matrix value by k_m f (2 b11 + b33)/(3 - f (2 L11 b11 + L33 b33)) with a positive denominator, so it exceeds k_m exactly when 2 b11 + b33 > 0, and filler whose Kapitza-corrected conductivities both exceed (both fall below) k_m raises (lowers) it. For spheres both Nan formulas reduce to Maxwell-Garnett with the Kapitza-corrected filler conductivity k/(1 + 2k/(G d)), which tends to k as G grows without bound, and the random value lies between the matrix and the corrected filler conductivity. The aligned axial Nan conductivity decreases strictly with L33 on [0, 1] and lies strictly between the series and parallel (Wiener) mixtures for L33 and f in (0, 1), so at fixed d3 it increases strictly with the aspect ratio. The Hasselman-Johnson formula is Maxwell-Garnett with the corrected conductivity at particle dimension d = 2 a_rad, so it agrees with the Nan sphere value under that radius-to-diameter conversion; it exceeds the matrix conductivity exactly above the critical radius (k_m/G) k/(k - k_m).
conditions: The filler is a dilute, monodisperse dispersion of identical axially symmetric spheroids in an isotropic matrix. Axis 3 is the symmetry axis and p = d3/d1 > 0, so p > 1 is prolate (fibre-like) and p < 1 is oblate (platelet-like). One interface conductance G_int > 0 applies to every face of every particle.

G_int is the interface conductance q_int/Delta T_int with q_int the heat flux across the interface and Delta T_int > 0 the temperature drop in the direction of that flux, so G_int is positive; the formulas add the series resistance 1/G_int once at each of the two interfaces a particle presents along a direction.

The catalog's d_1 and d_3 are full particle dimensions (the per-direction interface convention of Nan, Liu, Lin and Li, Appl. Phys. Lett. 85, 3549 (2004)), so a sphere has d equal to its diameter, while Hasselman-Johnson's a_rad is the sphere radius. The two formulas agree for spheres with d_1 = d_3 = 2 a_rad. Inserting the radius into d doubles the interface penalty 1/kc - 1/k = 2/(G_int d), from 1/(G_int a_rad) to 2/(G_int a_rad).

k_f[1,1] is the filler conductivity transverse to axis 3 and k_f[3,3] the conductivity along axis 3 (in-plane and through-plane for a platelet). The sphere reductions require k_f[1,1] = k_f[3,3], d_1 = d_3 and L11 = L33 = 1/3; the Hasselman-Johnson formula reads only k_f[3,3].

Random means isotropic three-dimensional orientation of the particles. Platelets oriented randomly within a plane are described by neither the random nor the aligned formula. The aligned operator is the component along the alignment axis 3, which is the through-plane direction only for platelets.
f_vol is the filler volume fraction in [0, 1], not a mass fraction or a percentage. Conductivities, G_int and particle dimensions are positive and use one coherent unit system.

Strict monotonicity of the aligned value in L33 and the strict Wiener bounds require 0 < f_vol < 1 and a Kapitza-corrected filler conductivity different from k_m; the aspect-ratio monotonicity varies p through L33 with d3, and so the axial Kapitza correction, held fixed. The critical-radius result requires a filler more conductive than the matrix and f_vol > 0.

conventions.model_scope: Dilute effective-medium (Maxwell-Garnett, Nan, Hasselman-Johnson) conductivity of filled composites. Physlib has no effective-medium model, so these are local theorems about the OMAI formulas over Mathlib reals; no Physlib declaration is identified.

conventions.unit_embedding: Coherent SI: conductivities in W/(m K), G_int in W/(m^2 K), lengths in m; f_vol, p and the depolarization factors are dimensionless.
conventions.held_fixed: Temperature, filler shape and orientation distribution, and the interface conductance are fixed; the theorems vary one of f_vol, L33, G_int or a_rad at a time as stated, and the aspect-ratio monotonicity varies p at fixed d3.

conventions.reference_energy: Not applicable.
conventions.qpoint_weighting: Not applicable.

remaining_obligations: NEMD or measured producers of G_int and of the filler and matrix conductivities are not verified.

Away from p = 1 the catalog's per-direction interface correction k/(1 + 2k/(G_int d)) (Nan et al. 2004) is a slab approximation with no validated accuracy; Nan et al., J. Appl. Phys. 81, 6692 (1997) uses K_p/(1 + R K_p L_ii (2 + 1/p)/a_1), and the two agree only at p = 1.

The effective-medium formulas are dilute approximations. Particle interactions at high loading, percolation, clustering, porosity, polydisperse size or shape, and orientation distributions other than isotropic random or perfectly aligned are not covered.
L11 = (1 - L33)/2 is the catalog's auxiliary sum rule and is not proved; the transverse aligned component is not proved.
For non-spherical random filler no bound between the matrix and filler conductivities is proved beyond the sign result, and the Hashin-Shtrikman bounds are not proved.
Anisotropic filler conductivity tensors beyond the two diagonal values, face-dependent interface conductance and temperature dependence are not covered.

bindings.statement: For second-order force constants on the sites of a Physlib crystal with equal mixed partials, translation invariance and finite range, the index-permutation symmetry Phi_ij(-R) = Phi_ji(R) follows from the translation invariance, the OMAI dynamical matrix D_ij(q) = sum_R e^{i q.R} Phi_ij(R)/sqrt(M_i M_j) is Hermitian at every wavevector, and with the acoustic sum rule the Gamma-point matrix has at least three independent zero modes, the mass-weighted rigid translations.
conditions: Represent the crystal with Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal: a finitely generated abelian translation group, a finite nonempty unit cell and sites (cell, label), on which the translation action moves the cell and keeps the label. A mode index is a unit-cell label with a Cartesian axis, and Phi_ij(R) is the reference-cell component i against component j in cell R.

Force constants are real second derivatives of the lattice potential with equal mixed partials, invariant under every lattice translation, and the reference-cell interactions vanish outside a finite set of cells, so the catalog sum over all R is finite.
The phase e^{i R q} is exp(i q.pos(R)) for an additive embedding pos of the translations into Cartesian space, the catalog's cell-vector convention. Masses are positive and per unit-cell label.

The acoustic sum rule, sum over cells and labels of Phi_{(kappa,alpha),(kappa',beta)}(R) = 0, is a stated hypothesis for the Gamma-point result. Phonopy and other producers enforce it numerically; it is not derived here from a potential.

conventions.model_scope: Harmonic lattice dynamics. No anharmonic, non-analytic, electronic or numerical producer is modeled.
conventions.component_scope: Mode index (unit-cell label, Cartesian axis); one dynamical matrix per wavevector, with all tensor components kept.
conventions.normalization_basis: Mass weighting 1/sqrt(M_i M_j) with masses per unit-cell label; the lattice sum runs over the finite set of interacting cells closed under inversion.

conventions.unit_embedding: Coherent SI: force constants in J/m^2 (1 eV/Angstrom^2 = 16.02176634 J/m^2), masses in kg, lattice vectors in m and wavevectors in rad/m. These exact-real statements do not certify floating-point adapters.
conventions.held_fixed: Crystal, unit cell, masses, force constants and the lattice embedding are fixed; only the wavevector varies.
conventions.admissibility: Positive masses; real force constants with equal mixed partials, translation invariance and finite range. Phase convention: the catalog and the Lean definitions use the cell-vector phase e^{+i q.R}. Phonopy and phono3py use atom positions, D_ph = U^dagger D_cat U with U = diag(e^{i q.tau_kappa}). omega^2 and nondegenerate velocities agree; eigenvectors differ by e^{-i q.tau} and off-diagonal velocity-operator elements differ, so phonopy eigenvectors fed into the catalog's dD/dq give wrong velocities.
conventions.reference_energy: The static lattice energy and any constant potential offset do not enter second derivatives.
conventions.qpoint_weighting: No q-point weighting is involved; the Hermiticity holds at every wavevector and the zero modes at Gamma.

remaining_obligations: Finite-displacement, DFPT and potential-based force-constant producers (compute_force_constants[order=2], compute_fc2_finite_displacement) are interpreted inputs, not verified implementations; supercell folding of computed force constants and their symmetrization are not modeled.

Long-range force constants without a finite range, Ewald-summed dipole tails and the thermodynamic limit of an infinite sum are outside scope.

bindings.statement: On a differentiable eigenvector path, away from Gamma: for the dynamical matrix of a Physlib crystal and a differentiable normalized eigenvector path along the wavevector line q + s e_alpha with eigenvalue omega^2 > 0 at s = 0, the eigenvalue is differentiable and the OMAI group velocity e^dagger (dD/dq_alpha) e / (2 omega), with dD/dq_alpha the actual derivative of the catalog dynamical matrix, is a real number equal to d omega/d q_alpha (Hellmann-Feynman). A compiled monatomic chain gives the textbook a sqrt(K/M) cos(q a / 2).
conditions: DynamicalMatrix is the crystal dynamical matrix of the crystal-dynamical-matrix binding without the non-analytic correction, and dD/dq_alpha is its exact derivative sum_R i R_alpha e^{i q.R} Phi_ij(R)/sqrt(M_i M_j) along the Cartesian axis alpha.

Along the line q + s e_alpha the eigenvector e(s) is differentiable and normalized with real eigenvalue omega^2(s), and omega^2(0) > 0. A nondegenerate branch away from Gamma admits such a path by analytic perturbation theory; that existence is a hypothesis. Symmetry-enforced degeneracies are generic (transverse pairs along Gamma-X and Gamma-L), and at such points the eigenvector a code returns is not on the path: phonopy projects the velocity per direction and phono3py averages over degenerate sets and the q-star.

omega = sqrt(omega^2) is angular frequency; the velocity is in m/s when q is in rad/m. Velocities stored in Angstrom THz are already d omega/dq (1 Angstrom THz = 100 m/s, no 2*pi). The eigenvectors must be in the catalog's cell-vector phase convention.

The compiled monatomic chain (Physlib ofUnitCell Z Unit, nearest-neighbour longitudinal springs K, mass M, spacing a) has omega^2 = (2K/M)(1 - cos(q_x a)) and catalog velocity a sqrt(K/M) cos(q_x a / 2) on 0 < q_x a < pi. It is an exact model example, not a material fit.

bindings.statement: Let N be the sublattice of a finite Born-von Karman supercell of a Physlib crystal and fold the crystal force constants into the supercell, Phi_BvK(R) = sum_L Phi(R + L). At every wavevector q commensurate with the supercell (e^{i q.L} = 1 for every L in N), the supercell dynamical matrix at the corresponding character equals the OMAI dynamical matrix D(q). If the folded supercell is mechanically stable (its harmonic energy is never negative), D(q) is positive semidefinite there, so every solution of the OMAI dispersion relation has omega^2 >= 0 and a real frequency.
conditions: DynamicalMatrix is the crystal dynamical matrix of the crystal-dynamical-matrix binding, passed through identity_dm without the non-analytic correction, under the same force-constant conditions.

The supercell is the quotient of the translations by a sublattice N with finitely many cosets (periodic boundary conditions). Its force constants are the folded sums of the crystal force constants; mechanical stability is the hypothesis that the real harmonic energy sum u_a Phi_BvK,ab u_b of the supercell is never negative.

Only wavevectors commensurate with the supercell are covered. Incommensurate meshes are the normal case for BTE (for example a 4x4x4 force-constant supercell with a 19x19x19 kappa mesh), and Fourier interpolation of supercell force constants is exact only at commensurate q; nothing is stated at the other mesh points.

omega is the nonnegative square root of omega^2 on a stable supercell; imaginary modes of an unstable structure are excluded by the hypothesis, not removed. A compiled Einstein-spring ring on ofUnitCell (ZMod 3) Unit shows the stability hypothesis is satisfiable.

bindings.statement: For the same family, the isothermal curvature modulus V*(d2F/dV2)_T at the volume (dG/dp)_T selected by the windowed Gibbs energy equals -V/(dV/dp)_T read off the Gibbs energy alone. Its positivity is the stability premise F_VV>0, not a separate result.
conditions: Use the same finite family of full Nat harmonic occupation ensembles as the Cp binding: product counting measure, unweighted oscillator energies, dof=0 and phase-space unit=1, with static energy N_q*E_0(v) attached through an actual singleton ensemble before molar normalization.

Temperature T and primitive-cell volume v are positive. Every frequency is positive and C2 on an open positive-volume domain. Static energy E_0(v) is C2, arbitrary signed, and independent of temperature. No mode may have zero or imaginary frequency; an unmodified Gamma-centred grid with zero acoustic modes does not satisfy the premises.
Keep masses, composition, atom and q counts, reduced-q labels, uniform q weights and the Avogadro scale fixed, with one q mesh at every volume. Frequencies depend on volume only.

The volume family V(T,p) is differentiable at every point of a neighborhood of the evaluation point (T,p), stays in the model domain and satisfies F_V(T,V)+p=0 throughout that neighborhood, with F_VV>0 at the evaluation point. The implicit-function theorem supplies such a family through every stable stationary point; a pointwise stationarity equation alone is insufficient.

The Gibbs energy is the infimum of F(T,V)+pV over an open volume window (a,b) that contains the selected molar volume and lies in the model domain. The window selects the family when F_VV(T,V)>0 for every V in (a,b) and every T near the evaluation temperature: a scan certifies itself by this convexity of F+pV across the scanned interval. The selected volume must lie strictly inside the scanned range; EOS extrapolation beyond the scanned volumes is not covered. Every sufficiently narrow window around the selected volume also selects the family; a window that reaches another local minimum can select another branch, which is not covered.

Interpret K^qha(E_tot,S,omega) as the isothermal modulus of the actual molar Helmholtz surface at the selected volume and temperature, the faithful mirror of the Phonopy EOS B0. The adiabatic modulus K_S=K_T*C_P/C_V and static-only curvature are different quantities and are not this output.

The modulus is taken along the model's single hydrostatic volume coordinate. A fixed-shape lattice scan of a non-cubic crystal gives a fixed-shape modulus and a shape-relaxed path a Reuss-type modulus. The BulkModulus node is defined as the Voigt average of the elastic tensor; it is listed as the output association of this binding and is not a proof subject.

Embed model values coherently in SI: T in K, p in Pa, E_0 in J per primitive cell, molar F and G in J/mol of primitive cells, v in m^3, V_m in m^3/mol, alpha_V in 1/K, K_T in Pa and capacities in J/(mol K) or J/(m^3 K). Convert Angstrom^3 by 10^-30, serving GPa by 10^9 and eV by 1.602176634e-19 J/eV. These exact-real interpretations do not certify floating-point adapters.

bindings.statement: For the static-plus-harmonic Physlib ensemble, the temperature derivative of actual molar enthalpy along a local stable constant-pressure branch equals the OMAI Cp identity. Cv, volume, expansion and isothermal bulk modulus must belong to the same molar free-energy surface.
conditions: Use a finite heterogeneous family of full Nat harmonic occupation ensembles, product counting measure, unweighted oscillator energies, dof=0 and phase-space unit=1. Attach static energy N_q*E_0(v) through an actual singleton ensemble before molar normalization.

Temperature T and primitive-cell volume v are positive. Every frequency is positive and C2 on an open positive-volume domain. Static energy E_0(v) is C2, arbitrary signed, and independent of temperature.
Keep masses, composition, atom and q counts, reduced-q labels, uniform q weights and Avogadro scale fixed. Frequencies depend on volume but have no independent temperature dependence.

Use molar volume V_m=N_A*v. Let F_static_joint be the actual free energy after attaching the N_q*E_0(v) singleton, and F_harmonic_joint the unshifted harmonic free energy. Then F_mol=(N_A/N_q)*F_static_joint=N_A*E_0(v)+(N_A/N_q)*F_harmonic_joint. Evaluate all quantities at the same temperature and equilibrium volume, per mole of the same primitive cells, not per mole of atoms.

The supplied volume path is differentiable at the evaluation temperature and satisfies domain membership and F_V+p_ext=0 throughout a neighborhood, with constant external pressure. Require F_VV>0 at the evaluation point; the proved C2 regularity permits restriction to a stable neighborhood. A pointwise stationarity equation alone is insufficient.

Interpret expansion as V_m_prime/V_m and bulk modulus as the isothermal derivative V_m*F_VV. Cp is the derivative of actual molar internal energy plus p_ext*V_m along that path; Cv is the fixed-volume capacity of the same actual ensemble.

Convert cell Angstrom^3 by 10^-30 to m^3, canonical pressure eV/Angstrom^3 by 1.602176634e11 to Pa, and serving GPa by 10^9 to Pa. Static energies served in eV require 1.602176634e-19 J/eV. bindings.statement: For the static-plus-harmonic Physlib ensemble on a local stable constant-pressure branch, the heat-capacity-weighted mean of mode Gruneisen parameters, defined from the volume derivatives of the mode frequencies and weighted by the actual canonical mode heat capacities, equals the OMAI identity alpha_V*K/C_V_vol. Expansion, isothermal bulk modulus and volumetric heat capacity must belong to the same free-energy surface, temperature and equilibrium volume.
conditions: Use the same finite family of full Nat harmonic occupation ensembles as the Cp binding: product counting measure, unweighted oscillator energies, dof=0 and phase-space unit=1, with static energy N_q*E_0(v) attached through an actual singleton ensemble before molar normalization.

Temperature T and primitive-cell volume v are positive. Every frequency is positive and C2 on an open positive-volume domain. Static energy E_0(v) is C2, arbitrary signed, and independent of temperature. No mode may have zero or imaginary frequency; an unmodified Gamma-centred grid with zero acoustic modes does not satisfy the premises.

Keep masses, composition, atom and q counts, reduced-q labels, uniform q weights and the Avogadro scale fixed, with one q mesh at every volume. Frequencies depend on volume only. Each labelled branch must be followed continuously through band crossings; sorted band order is not sufficient.

Define the mode Gruneisen parameter as gamma_i(v)=-v*omega_i_prime(v)/omega_i(v) from the volume family itself. Define Gamma(T,v)=sum_i gamma_i*c_i/sum_i c_i, where c_i is the actual derivative-defined canonical heat capacity of mode i at fixed v. Gamma does not use expansion, bulk modulus, the branch, the free energy or the quotient alpha_V*K/C_V_vol.

Evaluate Gamma, expansion, bulk modulus and volumetric heat capacity at the same temperature and at the branch volume v_B=V_m/N_A, per the same primitive cell that carries E_0(v) and the phonon grid. Supplied static energies, volumes and phonons must refer to that one cell.

The supplied volume path is differentiable at the evaluation temperature and satisfies domain membership and F_V+p_ext=0 throughout a neighborhood, with constant external pressure. Require F_VV>0 at the evaluation point. A pointwise stationarity equation alone is insufficient.

Interpret ThermalExpansion as the volumetric coefficient V_m_prime/V_m along that path, BulkModulus as the isothermal modulus V_m*F_VV at the same temperature, and VolumetricHeatCapacity as sum(c)/(N_q*v) at fixed v, equal to C_V_mol/V_m. Linear expansion, adiabatic or elastic moduli, static-only curvature and constant-pressure capacities are not these inputs.

Use the volumetric form only. The molar form alpha_V*K*V_m/C_V_mol is equivalent only with V_m and C_V_mol per mole of the same primitive cells. An adiabatic modulus paired with C_V_vol gives Gamma*(1+alpha_V*Gamma*T), not Gamma.
Supporting result, not a separate subject: at every point of the model domain, without a branch, the temperature derivative of pressure at fixed volume equals Gamma*C_V_vol.
Gamma, every gamma_i and alpha_V may be negative or zero. No statement is made at T=0, where Gamma is a limit of a ratio of vanishing capacities.

bindings.statement: For every stiffness tensor with the first minor symmetry that stores positive energy for every nonzero symmetric strain, the catalog's Voigt bulk and shear moduli are positive and its Poisson ratio lies strictly between -1 and 1/2. For an isotropic tensor the Voigt contractions return the Lame values K = lam + 2 mu/3 and G = mu, positivity of both is equivalent to stability, and the catalog's Poisson ratio and Young's modulus are the Lame expressions lam/(2(lam + mu)) and mu(3 lam + 2 mu)/(lam + mu). For a cubic tensor the contractions return (C11 + 2 C12)/3 and (C11 - C12 + 3 C44)/5, the trace of the stress depends on the strain only through its trace with modulus K, so K is the stress-controlled bulk modulus, and with C12 <= C11 and C44 >= 0 the curvature V0 E''(V0) of the cell energy minimized over cell shape at each volume is K. Under uniform scaling of the cell without shape relaxation the curvature is the Voigt K for every tensor.
conditions: ElasticConstants is the full fourth-rank stiffness tensor C_abcd on Cartesian indices in one orientation. Voigt 6x6 storage is expanded with the minor symmetries before the catalog sums apply; Mandel or Kelvin storage, with its factors sqrt(2) and 2 on the shear block, must be converted first.
The Lean stress sigma = C : e is tensile-positive, the negative of the catalog's compressive-positive Stress node, consistent with compute_elastic_constants defining C = -d sigma_OMAI / d eps.

The stability results require the first minor symmetry C_abcd = C_bacd and positive strain energy for every nonzero symmetric strain. The isotropic results use C_abcd = lam d_ab d_cd + mu (d_ac d_bd + d_ad d_bc); the cubic results use Voigt constants C11, C12, C44 with the cube axes along the Cartesian axes.

The catalog's Poisson ratio and Young's modulus take BulkModulus then ShearModulus. For an anisotropic crystal, E and nu computed from its Voigt K and G are Voigt-polycrystal estimates, neither Voigt-Reuss-Hill averages nor single-crystal directional values.

The equation-of-state results evaluate compute_bulk_modulus_eos at the reference volume V0 of a linear-elastic cell with energy E0 + V0 * W(e) / 2, W(e) = sum_abcd C_abcd e_ab e_cd, and volumetric strain 3 s(V) with s(V) = (V/V0)^(1/3) - 1. The cubic result minimizes W over every symmetric strain of that trace; the uniform-scaling result uses e = s(V) delta without shape relaxation.

bindings.statement: The catalog's isothermal Kamal-Sourour cure time t(alpha) = int_{alpha_0}^{alpha} da/((1 - a)^n (k1 + k2 a^m)), k_i = A_i exp(-E_i/(N_A k_B T)), increases strictly with conversion below full cure and has derivative 1/rate. Near every interior cure time there is one inverse alpha(t), taking that time back to the conversion, that solves d alpha/dt = (k1 + k2 alpha^m)(1 - alpha)^n at every time of a neighbourhood, and every continuous local inverse solves the rate law. These are local statements, not a global solution of the rate law. The catalog's DiBenedetto relation maps conversions [0, 1] one to one and strictly increasingly onto [T_g0, T_ginf] for lambda > 0 and T_g0 < T_ginf, and for 0 < lambda < 1 and T_g0 < T_ginf it lies strictly below the linear interpolation at every interior conversion.
conditions: Isothermal cure at absolute temperature T in kelvin with A_1, A_2 >= 0 in 1/s, autocatalytic order m >= 0, any real order n, initial conversion alpha_0 >= 0, and either A_1 > 0 (which includes pure nth-order kinetics with A_2 = 0) or alpha_0 > 0 with A_2 > 0, so that the rate is positive from alpha_0 up to full cure; conversions lie in [alpha_0, 1).
Conversion is a fraction in [0, 1], not a percentage. E_1 and E_2 are activation energies per mole and enter through R = N_A k_B; an activation energy per molecule must not be divided by N_A again.

The rate law is the single-(1 - alpha)^n Kamal-Sourour form; diffusion control, a temperature-dependent maximum conversion and separate exponents on the two terms are other models. Isothermal Kamal values are meaningful only while T_g(alpha(t)) stays below the cure temperature, before vitrification.

The DiBenedetto results use the Pascault-Williams form with lambda > 0 and alpha in [0, 1]; monotonicity, the bijection and the strict comparison with the linear interpolation require T_ginf > T_g0, and the comparison also 0 < lambda < 1. T_g0, T_ginf and T_g are in kelvin, as the GlassTransitionTemperature node and its evaluator store them; the Pascault-Williams algebra commutes with shifts of the temperature scale, which is a remark about the formula, not a change of storage unit.

conventions.component_scope: Scalar degree of cure and glass transition temperature of one homogeneous thermoset.
conventions.normalization_basis: Conversion is the fraction of reacted groups in [0, 1]; activation energies are per mole.
conventions.frequency_convention: Not applicable; rate constants are in 1/s and enter only through the Arrhenius factors.
conventions.unit_embedding: Coherent SI: T, T_g0, T_ginf and T_g in K, A_i in 1/s, E_i in J/mol, N_A in 1/mol, k_B in J/K, t_cure in s; alpha, m, n and lambda are dimensionless.
conventions.held_fixed: Temperature is constant during the cure; the kinetic parameters and the DiBenedetto parameters are fixed.
conventions.admissibility: T > 0 and the parameter ranges in the conditions; conversions at or above 1 and negative conversions have no asserted interpretation.
conventions.reference_energy: Not applicable.
conventions.qpoint_weighting: Not applicable.
